h1: The 6 Best Space Heaters Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Space Heaters Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact space heaters priced well inside $100, compared on timers, remotes, safety cutoffs, noise and desk-to-bedroom fit.
summary: The Small Portable heater with a 1 to 12 hour timer is our top pick for people who want a remote and a schedule. The DREO is the most controlled heater of the group. The Amazon Basics is the cheap pick with a stated tip-over cutoff, and the Lasko MyHeat is the desk-sized option from a known heater brand.
intro: A budget of $100 is more than any heater in this ranking needs, and that is the first thing worth knowing. Every pick here sits in a bucket of $50 or less, which means the question is not how to spend the money but which cheap features are worth paying for. Spending the leftover on a bigger heater rarely helps, because plug-in models share one ceiling: the outlet.

So we ranked six small heaters by the things that change a winter evening: timers that end the session for you, remotes, quiet running, and safety cutoffs the listing really names. Marketing adjectives like rapid and efficient earned nothing by themselves. A feature that appears as a number, a mode count or a named protection earned points, and a feature that is merely implied did not.

products.name: Small Portable Space Heater for Indoor Use
products.verdict: Three heating modes, a remote and a 1 to 12 hour timer make it the easiest to live with.
products.description:
This compact heater stacks the conveniences that matter after the first hour: three heating modes, remote operation and a timer that runs from 1 to 12 hours. The timer is the underrated part, because it ends the session even if you fall asleep under a blanket.

It takes the top spot because no other heater in this group lists a timer with that range. The DREO has better temperature sensing on paper, but it lacks a stated schedule, and the Amazon Basics is simpler still. The compromise is that the listing names no tip-over cutoff.

It suits a bedroom or a reading corner where you want warmth for a fixed stretch. Confirm the safety cutoffs on the product page before relying on it unattended.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and reading corners that need a scheduled session.
products.skipIf: You require a heater with a named tip-over cutoff.

products.name: DREO Space Heater
products.verdict: 1500W with an NTC chipset aimed at accuracy, and a build marketed around safety.
products.description:
DREO pitches this unit on precision: a 1500W element, an NTC chipset for sensing temperature and a design it describes as unbreakable in safety terms. An NTC sensor is a thermistor whose resistance changes with heat, so the heater reacts to the actual air instead of guessing.

It finishes behind the Small Portable only on convenience. That model lists a timer and a remote, whereas the DREO listing here gives no schedule feature. Against the Lasko MyHeat it is the more serious room heater, since the Lasko is built for a single desk.

Choose it for a bedroom or study where steady warmth matters. The caveat is that the summary lists no remote, so expect to walk over to change the setting.
products.idealFor: Study or bedroom use where steady warmth beats gadgets.
products.skipIf: You want a scheduled timer or a remote.

products.name: Amazon Basics Ceramic Space Heater
products.verdict: Plain ceramic heat for under $25 with tip-over protection stated plainly.
products.description:
Amazon Basics offers a compact, portable ceramic heater with adjustable heating options and tip-over protection spelled out in the listing. Ceramic elements warm quickly and run cooler on the outside than old coil designs, which is why they dominate this price tier.

It ranks third because it is the cheapest in the group and still names its main safety cutoff, but it gives up the timer of the Small Portable and the sensing chip of the DREO. It outranks the Gaiatop because that listing speaks only in generalities.

A good match for a rental, a dorm or a guest room. The caveat is the spare settings, so plan to adjust it by hand as the room warms.
products.idealFor: Dorms, rentals and guest rooms on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want scheduling or remote adjustment.

products.name: Lasko MyHeat Personal Space Heater
products.verdict: A desk-sized personal heater from a long-established heater brand.
products.description:
The Lasko MyHeat is built to keep one person warm at work, not to heat a room. Its listing speaks of a personal space heater that is easy to use, which signals a small footprint for placing under or beside a desk.

It ranks fourth because the scope is narrow. The DREO and the Small Portable can tackle a room, while the MyHeat exists for a single seat. It beats the Gaiatop mini on brand track record, though the listing states no wattage, timer or remote.

It is right for a cold office, a cubicle or a drafty workstation. The caveat is range: it will warm you, not the room, so do not buy it for a bedroom.
products.idealFor: Offices and cubicles where only you need warmth.
products.skipIf: You plan to heat a bedroom or living room.

products.name: Space Heater, Portable Small Heater for Indoor Use, Quiet & Compact
products.verdict: Heats in about two seconds by its own claim and is pitched as quiet.
products.description:
This small heater advertises a 2 second start, a quiet running profile and safety protection functions. The two second claim refers to how fast the element begins producing warm air, which matters most for short bursts, like warming a bathroom before a shower.

It sits fifth because the listing states no wattage, thermostat or timer, and quiet is a claim without a decibel figure. It does outrank the Gaiatop since its safety line and the speed claim are at least specific.

Pick it for a nightstand or a bathroom shelf. The caveat is that a heater this small warms its immediate vicinity, so treat it as a spot heater rather than a primary source.
products.idealFor: Bathrooms and bedside tables that need quick spot warmth.
products.skipIf: You need a room heater with a thermostat.

products.name: Gaiatop Mini Space Heater
products.verdict: A tiny space-saving heater with a fast-heating pitch and little else stated.
products.description:
Gaiatop sells a mini heater with a compact, space-saving design and fast, efficient heating. That is the whole listing, which means the product is bought on size and price alone.

It lands last because every competitor here names at least one concrete feature: a timer, a sensor, a tip-over cutoff or a defined personal-heater role. The Gaiatop offers none of those in its summary, so the ranking reflects missing detail rather than proven weakness.

It works as a throwaway option for a desk drawer, a suitcase or an office. The caveat is verification: read the full product page for wattage and safety cutoffs before trusting it near anything flammable.
products.idealFor: Travel bags, desk drawers and occasional use.
products.skipIf: You need documented safety features or timers.

whatMatters.detail: A timer switches the heater off after a set period, which protects against falling asleep with it running. A range like 1 to 12 hours is flexible enough for both a quick warm-up and a full evening. Look for the range written out on the listing, since a bare timer function could mean a fixed two hours.

A tilt switch kills power if the heater falls, which is the single most important mechanical safeguard on a floor unit. Pets and vacuum cords knock heaters over more often than people admit. Search the listing for the phrase tip-over protection, since a general safety line may not include it.

A sensor such as the NTC chipset on the DREO lets a heater respond to actual room temperature and cycle off. Without one the element simply stays on, and the room overshoots. Check for the word thermostat or a named sensor, and treat a bare list of heat modes as a manual fixed output.

Small desk heaters warm the person next to them, while 1500W units can lift a whole bedroom. Buying the wrong one is the most common disappointment at this price. Look for wattage and any square footage claim, and be skeptical of a tiny body promising whole-room warmth.

Quiet is a marketing word until a decibel number backs it. Fans and clicking thermostats are what you actually hear, and a bedroom heater is judged by them at night. Look for a decibel figure on the page, and read owner feedback for fan hum when none is given.

faq.q: Will these heaters trip a breaker?
faq.a: A 1500W unit like the DREO draws most of a 15 amp circuit, so avoid running it with a hair dryer or microwave on the same line. Small units such as the Gaiatop draw far less, but check the wattage on the label.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with timers?
faq.a: They set a long timer and assume the room stays warm after it ends. On the Small Portable, shorter timers paired with a pre-warmed room work better than a 12 hour setting that wastes power on an empty room.

faq.q: Is the DREO worth choosing over the Amazon Basics?
faq.a: For daily bedroom or study use, yes, because the DREO lists a sensing chip and full 1500W output. For occasional use or a rental room, the Amazon Basics names its tip-over cutoff and costs less.

faq.q: How do I set up the Small Portable heater?
faq.a: Plug it directly into a wall outlet on a flat hard surface, install remote batteries if required, then pick a mode and set the timer. Keep it clear of bedding, since an open grille needs airflow to avoid hot spots.

faq.q: How do I clean a ceramic heater?
faq.a: Unplug it, wait for it to cool, and brush or vacuum the grille. Dust on the Amazon Basics or Lasko burns off with a faint smell if left, and thick buildup chokes airflow and can trigger an overheat shutoff.

faq.q: Can a tiny heater warm a bathroom?
faq.a: Briefly, yes. The quiet compact model with the two second start suits a short morning warm-up. Keep any heater away from water, never place it near a tub, and use it only in dry conditions.

finalTake: Choose the Small Portable if you want a remote and a long timer, and the DREO if you want the most controlled warmth. The Amazon Basics is the budget pick that names its safety cutoff, while the Lasko MyHeat is the desk-only answer. Whichever you buy, none of these needs the full $100.
